title: Gmail for freight brokers on Mac in 2026: templates, shortcuts and Lazur voice help

description: Gmail for freight brokers on Mac: web app setup, templates, keyboard shortcuts, attachment limits and shared inbox gaps. Plus voice help with Lazur.
targetKeyword: gmail for freight brokers on mac
intro: Gmail for freight brokers on Mac means the Gmail web app, open in Safari or Chrome. Google has no native Gmail app for Mac, according to Orbit's 2026 guide, so you work in the browser all day. This page covers the setup that saves the most time on a broker's inbox: templates, keyboard shortcuts, attachment limits and the shared-inbox gaps Gmail leaves open.
tldr: Use the Gmail web app in Safari or Chrome. No native Gmail app for Mac exists, per Orbit's 2026 guide.
Turn on templates from a computer: Settings > See all settings > Advanced > Templates > Enable.
Turn on keyboard shortcuts, then send the open message with ⌘ Enter.
A personal Gmail account caps attachments at 25 MB. Workspace limits come from your admin.
Gmail gives a shared inbox no collision alerts, so name one owner for every thread.

blocks.text: What Gmail for freight brokers on Mac means in practice

You open Gmail in your browser. Safari and Chrome both work. There is no Gmail download to install on a Mac. Orbit, a Mac mail vendor, says Google has never shipped a native Gmail app for Mac, and Google offers Gmail only as a web app. Google's own desktop help page did not load when we checked, so confirm this on Google's help center if it matters to your setup.

Orbit's 2026 guide lists four routes. A Chrome app shortcut is free. Apple Mail over IMAP works, but it drops Google-specific features such as Calendar, Drive and Meet. Mimestream and other paid wrappers exist too, so check their pricing pages before you pay.

For most brokers the browser version is the right call. You keep Calendar, Drive and Meet under one login. Pin it to the Dock so it opens in its own window. The steps are in [how to pin Gmail to the Dock](/how-to/pin-gmail-to-the-dock-in-gmail).
Why the inbox fills up so fast

Freight email runs on volume. FreightWaves reported in May 2024 that C.H. Robinson receives over 11,000 emails a day asking for truckload pricing. Your own count will be smaller. The pattern is the same. Quote requests, capacity offers and coverage updates all land in one inbox.
Capacity makes it worse. Truckstop's H1 2026 outlook says 86% of brokers find capacity has gotten tougher. Harder capacity means more carrier emails, more calls and more replies to track.
Most of the day falls into four kinds of email.

items: Shipper quote requests. They need a rate and a fast reply.
Carrier capacity offers. They need a yes or no, often within the hour.
Load coverage updates. They need a status and a next step.
Follow-ups on quotes and calls that went quiet.

blocks.text: Set up Gmail templates for repeat freight emails

Templates are the built-in tool that fits this job best. You have to switch them on first. Google says templates are enabled on computer only. Go to Settings (gear icon, top right) > See all settings > Advanced > Templates, choose Enable, then click Save Changes.

Build each template from a real email you already sent. Write it in Compose, then open More options > Templates > Save draft as template > Save as new template. Give it a name you will recognize, such as Quote follow-up.

items: Write the message in Compose with the structure you want.
Click More options > Templates > Save draft as template.
Choose Save as new template, then name it.
Next time, open Compose, then More options > Templates > Insert template.

blocks.text: A freight email guide from F5-Out lists nine shipper-facing templates, and it gives timing for each one. It gives no reply rates or time savings, so treat it as a starting list, not proof.

rows: The first contact with a new shipper
When you have capacity to offer a shipper on a lane
Within one hour of the call
24 hours after a quote with no response
3 to 6 months after they went quiet
After a load goes well and the shipper is happy
blocks.caption: Nine shipper templates and their timing, from F5-Out's freight broker guide.

blocks.text: Start with three: first touch, after a quote, and the follow-up. Add the rest once those feel routine.

blocks.title: Overwriting deletes the old text
blocks.text: Google's help page says an existing template can be overwritten, and deleted templates cannot be recovered. Paste the old text into a note before you save over it or delete it.
Insert a template and check every number before you send
Open Compose, then choose More options > Templates > Insert template. The text drops into the body. Then check each field. Lane, rate, pickup window and equipment type change from load to load.
The common mistake is sending last week's numbers. A shipper who reads an old rate may think you quoted it. Read the body once before you press ⌘ Enter.
Follow one quote thread from first email to follow-up
Here is how one quote thread looks when you use templates and a label. The timing follows the F5-Out guide. Your shop may run on a different schedule.

items: Monday: send the quote, then label the thread Quote follow-up.
Tuesday, no reply: insert the after-a-quote template and send it.
Later: insert the follow-up template when its window arrives.
Still quiet: send the final follow-up, then move the thread out of the label.

blocks.text: Use a filter to send a template as an automatic reply

Gmail can send a template for you. Create a filter, check Send template, choose the template, then click Create filter. Matching mail gets the reply when it arrives. Use this for mail that needs the same acknowledgement every time, such as a receipt for a capacity offer.

Keep it narrow. An auto reply to an automated sender creates noise on both sides. Test the filter on one known sender first. The full steps are in [how to create a filter in Gmail](/how-to/create-a-filter-in-gmail).
Keyboard shortcuts for Gmail on a Mac

Shortcuts are off until you switch them on. Open Settings > See all settings, turn on Keyboard shortcuts, then click Save Changes. Google uses ⌘ for the Mac Command key, so ⌘ Enter sends the open message.

items: ⌘ Enter sends the message you are writing.
Shift + / opens the full shortcut list in Gmail.
Shortcuts live in Gmail settings, not in macOS System Settings.
If a key does nothing, check that your cursor is not in a text field.

blocks.text: Learn three shortcuts a week, not thirty at once. Start with send, then the shortcut list, then the one you press most. Your hands catch up faster than you expect.
Attachment limits and the 25 MB rule

A personal Gmail account caps attachments at 25 MB. On Google Workspace, your administrator sets the attachment limits. Workspace also limits how much mail an account can receive. It allows up to 500 attachments per email, and message size up to 50 MB on Enterprise Standard or 70 MB on Enterprise Plus.

Message size counts after encoding, and encoding adds about 37%. On a Workspace account with the Enterprise Standard limit, take a 35 MB scan of a signed bill of lading. After encoding it is about 48 MB, close to the 50 MB limit. Add a 5 MB photo and the total reaches about 55 MB, which is over the limit.

items: Upload it to Google Drive and send the link instead.
Split a long PDF into two parts, named Part 1 of 2 and Part 2 of 2.
Lower the scan resolution before you attach it.

blocks.text: Ask your admin for the Workspace number before a busy week. Write it on your checklist. The attach steps are in [how to attach a file in Gmail](/how-to/attach-a-file-in-gmail).
The shared inbox gap: who owns this thread?

Many shops share one mailbox so dispatchers can cover for each other. Google Groups offers a collaborative inbox for that job. An Emailmeter article on Google Groups says replies go out from each member's own account. Team members work the mailbox in the Google Groups view, not in Gmail.

The same article says there is no alert when a colleague is already typing a reply. It also says there is no alert when a message goes unanswered. Two people can answer the same carrier, and nobody gets warned.

blocks.title: Name the owner in the subject
blocks.text: Put the owner's initials in the subject line, such as Covering: initials. Everyone sees who holds the thread before they type.

items: Put the shipper or carrier name and the load number in the subject line.
Label each thread with the dispatcher who owns it. The steps are in [how to create a label in Gmail](/how-to/create-a-label-in-gmail).
Only the owner replies. Others add a note in the thread instead.
Star a thread when a reply is owed. Unstar it once you send.
Test the rule on one thread before the whole team adopts it.

blocks.text: What the numbers do and do not show

C.H. Robinson says its AI reply supplies a truckload quote in an average of two minutes 13 seconds, per FreightWaves. That is a large carrier running its own system. It is not a benchmark for a Gmail inbox.

No independent study measures how much time Gmail templates save a broker. F5-Out gives no reply rates either. Measure your own week instead. Track the time to first reply, and count the follow-ups you sent late.

Adoption is still uneven. A 2026 Truckstop and Bloomberg Intelligence survey of 141 brokers found 48% deploying AI or machine-learning productivity tools. The sample leans toward independent brokers and mid-market 3PLs, so large shops may look different.
Where Lazur fits while you work in Gmail

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. It is not a plugin, and it does not run inside Gmail. You keep working in your browser, and Lazur helps by voice. It listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut.

Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where something is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click. Lazur does not click buttons for you.
Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Long follow-ups go faster when you speak them. Snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots are included.

Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, on the Mac. It runs on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. [Download Lazur](/download) to try it.
Mistakes that cost brokers time in Gmail

items: Sending a template with last week's lane or rate.
Overwriting a template without copying the old text first.
Leaving keyboard shortcuts off, then clicking Send every time.
Attaching a large file when a Drive link would do.
Setting a filter on automated mail, then getting auto replies back.
Two people answering one carrier because nobody owns the thread.

blocks.text: Most of these come from skipping one check. Read the subject line and the first lines before you act. The check takes seconds, and it stops most bad sends.
A day-one setup checklist for Gmail on your Mac

items: Open Gmail in Safari or Chrome and pin it to the Dock.
Turn on Templates under Settings > See all settings > Advanced.
Turn on keyboard shortcuts under Settings > See all settings.
Save your first three templates: first touch, after a quote, and the follow-up.
Ask your admin for the attachment limits if you run Workspace.
Agree on one owner rule for the shared inbox before the first busy morning.

blocks.text: Sources and what we could not confirm

Google's desktop help page did not load when we checked, so the no-native-app claim rests on Orbit, a competing Mac Gmail client. Google's template page does not state a maximum number of templates, so this page lists none.

No independent study of broker Gmail pain points was found. The slow parts above come from Gmail's documented limits and one vendor article. Mobile template support was not verified, so this page does not cover it.

faq.question: Is there a Gmail app for Mac?
faq.answer: Not a native one. Orbit's 2026 guide says Google has never shipped a Gmail app for Mac and offers Gmail only as a web app. Use Gmail in Safari or Chrome, or add a Chrome app shortcut. Mail apps over IMAP exist, but they drop Google features such as Calendar, Drive and Meet.

faq.question: Can I use Gmail templates on my iPhone?
faq.answer: Google's setup steps say templates are enabled on computer only. The help page does not cover phone apps, so test templates on your phone before you rely on them there.

faq.question: How many templates can I save in Gmail?
faq.answer: Google's template help page does not state a maximum. Save the set you use each week, then check that each one inserts correctly.

faq.question: Why do my Gmail keyboard shortcuts not work?
faq.answer: Shortcuts are off until you turn them on. Go to Settings > See all settings, choose Keyboard shortcuts on, and click Save Changes. Then press Shift + / to see the full list.

faq.question: What is the attachment limit for a freight broker?
faq.answer: A personal Gmail account allows a 25 MB attachment limit. On Workspace, your admin sets the limits. Workspace also allows up to 500 attachments per email and message size up to 50 MB on Enterprise Standard.

faq.question: Can Lazur send my email for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, so you press ⌘ Enter yourself. Lazur can type a draft at your cursor, and you read it before you send.

faq.question: Does Lazur send my email content to AI providers?
faq.answer: Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. Lazur listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Does Gmail warn you when a teammate is replying?
faq.answer: Not in a Google Groups shared inbox. A vendor article says there is no alert when a colleague is typing or when a message goes unanswered. Set an owner rule for each thread.
